description:
crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:228 — Dispatcher::dispatch signature:

    pub async fn dispatch(
        &self,
        request: JmapRequest,
        caller: CallerCtx,
        session_state: State,
    ) -> JmapResponse

Returns a JmapResponse — the wire-format response and nothing else.
The internal loop in lib.rs:239-313 tracks information that's
useful to a production consumer but that the return type cannot
surface:

- Whether any handler panicked (lib.rs:302-311 maps panics to
  serverFail invocations, but the dispatcher caller can't tell
  the difference between "this method returned serverFail
  legitimately" and "this method panicked and was caught").
- Per-method timing (used for tracing/observability).
- Whether ResultReference resolution failed for any method
  (currently maps to an error invocation; same as panic — wire
  shape merges error origins).
- The count of handlers whose `caller_clone` was actually used
  (vs cloned and discarded due to early errors).

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That observability data about a dispatch will be surfaced. A
   consumer that needs to emit `dispatch_panics_total{}` for SRE
   alerting cannot get the panic flag from the response — they
   must parse the response's methodResponses and pattern-match
   on `"type": "serverFail"` with the static description string.
   That pattern-match is brittle: it catches legitimate
   serverFails too.

2. That metrics can be added later without a major bump. Adding
   a fourth field to the returned tuple (e.g. (JmapResponse,
   DispatchMetrics)) breaks every existing call site.

3. That a wrapper layer in consumer code is the only place
   metrics can land. The wrapper has to do the same response-
   walking pattern-match the dispatcher already did internally
   — duplicate work.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

- Every production consumer rolls its own observability wrapper
  around dispatch(), duplicating the kit's internal classification
  logic. Either:
   a. They get the panic detection right (rare in practice —
      legitimate serverFails get counted as panics)
   b. They get it wrong silently.
- Future kit features (per-call deadline, cancellation token,
  request-scoped tracing context) can't be added at the
  dispatch layer because there's no return-shape slot for
  signalling outcome to the caller.

Resolution paths (one is sufficient):

- Wrap the return type in a #[non_exhaustive] struct:

    pub struct DispatchOutcome {
        pub response: JmapResponse,
        // future fields: dispatch_panics: usize, total_handler_time: Duration, etc.
    }
    pub async fn dispatch(...) -> DispatchOutcome;

  This is the analogue of finding ↑ JMAP-jfia.19 for HandlerFuture
  output. Same rationale: the kit's first major bump is the right
  time to convert "single anonymous return" into "named-struct
  return".

- Provide a separate observation API: `dispatch_with_observer(...,
  observer: impl DispatchObserver) -> JmapResponse`. The observer
  trait has method hooks for panic-occurred, method-started,
  method-completed, etc. Consumers wire their telemetry to the
  observer. The single-arg dispatch keeps working for consumers
  that don't care.

- Surface a parallel `tracing::span!` instrumentation inside
  dispatch under a `tracing` Cargo feature, so consumers wire
  their tracing subscriber and get the data via the tracing
  ecosystem. (Adds a dep, but tracing is already in the kit's
  dependency neighborhood implicitly through tokio.)

The cleanest is the first option (DispatchOutcome struct). It
matches the existing #[non_exhaustive] policy in the workspace
AGENTS.md and aligns with finding JMAP-jfia.19's recommendation
for the handler return shape.
title: Dispatcher::dispatch returns JmapResponse with no surface for per-call metrics, panic flag, or handler timings
